t: Traced to Gorm the Old around 936, Denmark is among the oldest continuous monarchies in the world.
Its kings ruled England under Cnut, led the Kalmar Union of 1397 and taxed Baltic shipping through the Sound Toll.
Defeats by Sweden in 1658 and by Prussia and Austria in 1864 left a small state that rebuilt itself as a welfare democracy.
dyk: The Royal Law of 1665, which made the Danish king absolute, was not published until 1709 and is often called the only written constitution of European absolutism.
ev: Harald Bluetooth adopts Christianity and raises the great Jelling stone
Valdemar II wins at Lyndanisse and establishes Danish rule in northern Estonia
Margaret I unites Denmark, Norway and Sweden in the Kalmar Union
Christian III introduces the Lutheran Reformation
The Treaty of Roskilde cedes Scania, Halland and Blekinge to Sweden
The Treaty of Kiel transfers Norway to Sweden
The Constitution of 5 June ends absolute monarchy
Defeat in the Second Schleswig War costs Schleswig and Holstein

f.capital: Jelling; later Roskilde; Copenhagen from the 15th century
